title: Canary Health Inspector — journey & wireframe notes
content:
Purpose: capture a working draft for the Canary Health Inspector flow — focused on surfacing real-time canary health signals, making automatic fallback/stop decisions visible, and giving operators a compact investigative experience. This doc mixes user-journey prose, low-fi wireframe notes, and a short grooming backlog.

Context and problem:
- We already have traffic-split controls and staged rollouts in the console, but users report difficulty understanding *why* a canary was aborted or rolled back automatically.
- Current telemetry is fragmented across model dashboards and route-level traces; people open multiple tabs to piece together the picture.
- Aim: a single inspector panel that surfaces the canary state, key signals (latency, error rate, model-quality-drift), and a timeline of automated policy actions with quick manual override.

Goals (observer-centric):
1) Make automated fallback decisions auditable and explainable.
2) Reduce mean-time-to-diagnose (MTTD) for canary regressions to < 10 minutes.
3) Provide actionable remediation hints (rollback, throttle, adjust split, pin model).
4) Keep the UI compact enough to be embedded inside the rollout details page and available as a full-screen inspector.

Success metrics (proposed):
- % of canary fallback incidents where operator can identify root cause within 10m (survey metric).
- Reduction in follow-up support tickets referencing "unknown rollback" by 70% in first quarter.
- Adoption: > 40% of active rollout ops click into Inspector at least once during a rollout.

Personas:
- Platform Engineer (SRE-ish): cares about end-to-end latency, error surfaces, and traffic-level patterns. Wants logs and traces links.
- Product Engineer (model owner): cares about model quality regression signals, token-level rejects, hallucination alerts. Wants quick rollback and notes.
- Customer Success/Support: wants readable timeline and human-friendly summary for customer postmortems.

High-level journey (operator enters from rollout detail):
1) Click "Open Canary Inspector" or hover quick-preview.
2) Inspector top summary: canary state (running/paused/aborted), current traffic split, age, and short human summary (auto-aborted by policy X at T).
3) Signal bar: compact sparklines for latency p50/p95, error rate, throughput, and divergence score. Each sparkline is tappable to expand a 1h/6h/24h tiled chart.
4) Timeline: ordered list of events (policy-eval triggers, manual actions, metric spikes). Each event expands to show raw metric snapshot + links to traces/segments.
5) Policy card: shows the automatic fallback policy that evaluated (thresholds, lookback window, severity). Buttons: "Simulate" (run policy on historical window), "Edit policy" (route to policy editor), "Override" (manual action).
6) Investigation pane: logs + top suspect traces + sample requests. For privacy, show hashed request ids, and provide link to customer-managed S3 if available.
7) Quick actions: rollback (with reason input), stop canary, reduce split to X% with suggested value, pin previous model version. Actions require confirmation modal and offer immediate timeline annotation.

Wireframe notes (low-fi panels):
- Header: route name, canary name, elapsed time, traffic split slider (live control but requires confirmation). Small badge for "Auto-fallback enabled".
- Left column (60%): big timeline + expanded chart area. Top of column shows a 3-line human summary generated from policy evaluation logic (automatic sentence).
- Right column (40%): policy card(s) stacked, quick actions, and recent alerts list.
- Compact mode: used in rollout list — shows state, a micro-timeline sparkline, and the primary failing metric.

Policy evaluation visibility: what to show to satisfy explainability without overwhelming:
- Decision provenance: which rule fired, exact threshold, snapshot values (e.g., p95=684ms, threshold=550ms), lookback window.
- Confidence indicator for model-quality signals (high/medium/low) — computed from eval-set sample size.
- Suggested next steps (auto-generated): e.g., "Reduce split to 10% and re-evaluate after 15m", "Rollback to v3.1.2 if error rate remains > 2% for 10m".

Design tradeoffs / open questions:
- How much raw telemetry should be embedded vs linked out? (performance vs completeness). Proposal: show 1h inline, link to full traces + long-term dashboards.
- Do we surface request payload samples in the inspector? Security/privacy concerns — default off, opt-in via role or project policy.
- Where to store and show audit records? We need timeline annotations to be immutable once actioned (or record who and when changed).

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Flaky metric ingestion: show "stale data" state and fall back to last-known-good. Provide a readability hint when sample size < N.
- Partial outages in region: show per-region breakdown and allow region-scoped stop.
- Policy cascading: multiple policies may trigger (latency + quality). Show prioritized cause and let operator expand both.

Backlog (groomed tasks, rough estimates):
- RNWR-432: Inspector MVP skeleton + routing from rollout detail (1 sprint) — owner: Miguel.
- RNWR-436: Policy card UI + simulate button + provenance display (2 sprints) — owner: Priya.
- RNWR-441: Compact inspector embed for rollout list + micro-sparkline (0.5 sprint) — owner: Leah.
- RNWR-448: Sample request redaction and opt-in privacy toggle (1 sprint) — owner: Omar.
- RNWR-455: Automated annotations & immutable audit trail (1.5 sprint) — owner: Ava.

Proposed copy and microcopy examples:
- Automatic summary: "Auto-aborted: p95 latency exceeded 550 ms (684 ms) over 10m window; fallback executed to stable model v3.1.2."
- Confirm modal for rollback: "Rolling back to v3.1.2 will redirect 100% of traffic to the stable model. Add a short reason for the audit log (optional)."

Security / permissions:
- Inspector view: read for most product teams. Quick actions (rollback/pin) gated by role: rollout-admin or owner.
- Policy edit: only editable by policy-admin role. Simulate allowed for read+ roles.

Next steps (practical):
1) Sync with Observability eng to finalize which metrics are cheap to fetch for inline 1h view.
2) Design sketches (hi-fi) from Leah after this doc lands — aim for 2 variants: compact and full-screen.
3) PO approval on the three policy-explainability fields to display (threshold snapshot, sample size, confidence).
4) Post-merge: small user study with 6 early adopter customers to validate that summaries are understandable and that actions reduce confusion.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas:
- Consider a "why-it-failed" NLP summary that pulls from metric snapshots and policy text — short and human-readable. Prototype could be a serverless function that returns a single sentence.
- Add a keyboard shortcut to open inspector from any rollout page (power user convenience).

Slack threads / refs: #rollouts-console, #observability, convo thread: <https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02ABC123/p1692048000000>.

Open questions for PM review (explicit):
- Do we want simulation runs to be stored historically (helpful for audits) or ephemeral? Recommendation: store last 5 simulations per rollout.
- Should policy edits be versioned and visible in the timeline? Recommendation: yes, versioned with links to the config diff.

Quick sketch checklist for next design pass:
- [ ] Hero summary sentence generator text states defined.
- [ ] Sparkline interactions mapped to chart zoom levels.
- [ ] Policy provenance UI microcopy finalized.
- [ ] Audit modal and reason input design.
- [ ] Error / stale-data states designed.

End of draft.

Revision history:
- 2024-08-15: initial notes and rough journey (Ava).
- 2024-08-20: added backlog lines and policy card draft (Miguel, Priya).
- 2024-08-28: updated open questions and privacy notes post-observability sync (Leah, Omar).
